sub_scenario.one_line: insurance claims trainer: keep preparation asynchronous or limit it to one short sync

dialogue.content: I spent the first hour tidying the insurance claims trainer and closing stale entries.
Anything still open?
Two items, both with owners.
The calendar review wrapped early today.
Any surprises in it?
None worth recording.
I can lead one short video update about claims rehearsal without trouble. Case-note 457.
A single check-in is different from stacked rehearsal. Case-note 458.
It does not leave my voice strained. Case-note 459.
Someone new shadowed me in the workplace this morning.
Did that slow you down?
A little, but the questions were good ones.
I batched my replies about the review cycle into one message before lunch.
Cleaner than drip-feeding answers.
Much cleaner.
I did a standard pass over the calendar records this morning.
Any exceptions in there?
None worth a note.
Written review of claims rehearsal keeps my preparation clear. Case-note 460.
Preparation need not be lens-on. Case-note 461.
I can use a offline script instead. Case-note 462.
I archived last cycle's notes on the calendar and set up the new folder.
A fresh start?
As fresh as these things get.
I confirmed next week's calendar slots with the team.
Any conflicts?
None that survived five minutes.
A vendor call about the insurance claims trainer ran long but ended well.
Worth the time?
This one, yes.
I walked through the workplace checklist with the new starter.
How did they do?
Careful and quick, a good sign.
Quiet afternoon; I cleared the backlog around the review cycle.
A rare day.
I did not waste it.
I flagged a small inconsistency in the calendar records and fixed it at the source.
Root cause or symptom?
Root cause, for once.
I closed a routine review cycle cycle without surprises.
Follow-up needed?
A note for the next cycle, nothing more.
I sketched next week's plan for the review cycle before leaving.
Ahead of schedule?
Ahead enough to sleep well.
Lunch walk, then a clean pass through the insurance claims trainer updates.
Does the walk help?
It resets the afternoon.
I moved my reminders so the insurance claims trainer review lands before the weekly sync.
Small automation helps.
It adds up over a quarter.
I compared two options for the calendar tooling and noted a mild preference.
Decision made?
Deferred until the trial ends.
I closed the week by updating the workplace handover notes.
Anything unusual to hand over?
Blessedly little.
The project manager asks for two consecutive Wednesday camera rehearsals before Thursday's broker briefing. What should I answer?
